one_liner: Z80/8080-family C toolchain (sccz80, zsdcc, z80asm) whose assembly C and maths libraries run 1.1-5.4x fewer cycles than stock SDCC 4.6.0.
what_it_does: A cross-development kit for 8080, 8085, Z80, Z80N, Z180, eZ80, Rabbit, Game Boy and related CPUs, with built-in support for over 100 machines. The zcc front end drives one of several C compilers: sccz80 (Small-C lineage, near C90), zsdcc (z88dk's patched SDCC) or the experimental 80cc. It then calls z80asm, a relocatable macro assembler, linker and librarian, and appmake, which writes tape, disk, ROM or hex images. You pick a target (+zx, +cpm, +z80, +test ...), a compiler and one of two C library worlds, classic or newlib, whose headers and CRTs differ. It is not a drop-in for the sdcc command line, but the same C sources compile with small changes (the benchmarks only swap the timer-label macro).
how_it_is_fast: Most of the speed comes from the libraries, not the compilers. The C standard library and the float and 32-bit integer runtimes are hand-written Z80 assembly, while SDCC ships C-implemented float and long routines (the wiki blames SDCC's losses on these). math32 is an assembly IEEE-754 single-precision package. It uses an unrolled 32_24x8 software mantissa multiply on a plain Z80, the hardware multiplies on Z80N, Z180, eZ80 and Rabbit, and a Quake magic-number seed plus three Newton-Raphson steps for sqrt. Its add and subtract use a cheaper jam-sticky rounding rule instead of round-to-nearest-even. The newlib 'fast integer' build reduces most 32-bit divides to 16-bit divides. zsdcc also uses the __z88dk_callee and __z88dk_fastcall calling conventions to pass arguments to library calls more cheaply.
when_to_use: Float-heavy C on a Z80 (physics, Whetstone-style maths). With math32, n-Body runs in 0.81-0.86 G cycles against 4.36 G for SDCC 4.6.0 (5.1-5.4x) and 1.60 G for HI-TECH C 7.80 (about 2x).
32-bit integer arithmetic such as bignum-style division loops. The classic sccz80 library runs Pi in 1.99 G cycles against SDCC's 7.22 G (3.6x) in the default configuration.
Retro and homebrew machines (ZX Spectrum, Spectrum Next, CP/M, MSX, RC2014, RomWBW, Game Boy), where z88dk's built-in targets, CRTs and appmake output formats save porting work.
8080 and 8085 targets, where sccz80 and 80cc are the supported compilers (zsdcc is Z80-only) and math32_8085 and mbf32 cores exist.
Mixed C and assembly projects that want one assembler, linker and librarian (z80asm) with sections, macros and multi-CPU fat libraries.
when_not_to_use: Allocation-heavy code on the newlib library. Binary-Trees takes 6.57 G cycles against SDCC's 0.19 G (about 34x slower) because newlib malloc's first-fit search walks allocated blocks too. Issue #113 has been open since 2017; use the classic library (149 M cycles, 1.30x faster than SDCC) for such code.

Tight integer loop code compiled with sccz80. On Sieve its builds take 4.67-4.96 M cycles against SDCC's 4.22 M, and on Fannkuch 67-77 M against 55.7 M. Only zsdcc with newlib wins, by 1.15x and 1.06x, and HI-TECH C 7.80 is fastest on Fannkuch.
Code-size-critical builds that assume z88dk is always smaller. SDCC is smallest on Sieve and Dhrystone, HI-TECH C is smallest on Fannkuch, and math32 rows are larger than the older 48-bit rows.
Projects that need strict IEEE-754 float semantics. math32 flushes denormals to signed zero, does not use round-to-nearest-even on add and subtract, and does not propagate NaN payloads.
Projects that need an OSI-approved licence. The Clarified Artistic License is FSF-free but not OSI-approved, and individual files may carry other licences.

integration.form: cross toolchain (compilers, z80asm assembler/linker and prebuilt target libraries statically linked into the output binary)
integration.dependencies: Host side: prebuilt Windows and macOS nightlies, a Linux Snap, a Docker image, or a source build that needs git submodules (m4 is used for the macro pass). Target side: none beyond the chosen z88dk library.
integration.min_toolchain: Not documented in the pages read for building from source. On the target side, sccz80 accepts near-C90 C and zsdcc accepts SDCC's larger C subset.
integration.platforms: Hosts: Windows, macOS, Linux. Target CPUs: 8080/8085, KR580VM1, gbz80, Z80, Z80N, Z180, eZ80 (Z80 mode), R800, Rabbit r2ka-r6k and KC160. Classic library targets cover more than 100 machines.
integration.thread_safety: math32 says all of its code is re-entrant. Re-entrancy of the rest of the C library is not documented in the pages read.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — zsdcc is the same SDCC 4.6.0 front end, but you build through zcc with a target, a -clib choice and z88dk headers. It uses __sdcccall(0) with z88dk callee/fastcall conventions, not stock SDCC's __sdcccall(1), so linking against objects from stock SDCC is not documented.

gotchas: Harness flaw in the baseline rows. All eight SDCC readmes (n-Body, Pi, Whetstone, Dhrystone, Fasta, Binary-Trees, Sieve, Fannkuch) derive TIMER_START and TIMER_STOP from .sym and .map values by hand, and in every one the documented arithmetic gives a different address from the one passed to z88dk-ticks. Examples: n-Body works out to 0xd83/0xdcc but ran with 0d7a/0dc0; Pi to 0x213/0x32e but ran with 0214/0363; Whetstone's stop to 0xbde but ran with 09ca, a window 532 bytes shorter. z88dk-ticks (cpu_run in src/ticks/ticks.c) resets its counter every time PC equals -start and halts the first time PC equals -end, so a wrong address silently changes the measured window. The z88dk rows look up the symbols from the map file (-x map -start TIMER_START), which avoids this. The counts are not at the -counter cap and their sizes look plausible, but the baseline windows cannot be checked without rebuilding.

Rows are not all like for like. Whetstone and Fasta were timed with SDCC built without -DSTATIC, while every z88dk build used -DSTATIC (static rather than stack locals). Unlabelled z88dk float rows use 48-bit genmath or math48, which zsdcc narrows to 4 bytes. The newlib *_FAST Pi rows need the z80 library rebuilt with __CLIB_OPT_IMATH=75, which is not the default. The wiki's sccz80 newlib Pi rows quote April 2020 counts (4,012,440,735 and 1,696,878,309) even though the readme has slower April 2022 remeasures (4,028,061,102 and 1,766,815,709).

Since v2.5, -lm links math32 instead of genmath (classic) or math48 (newlib). Old build lines therefore change float width and precision silently; use --genmath, --math48 or --mbf64 to get the wider formats back.

All cycle counts come from the project's own z88dk-ticks emulator, and the wall-clock columns are cycles divided by 4 MHz. The HI-TECH C and IAR rows were also run by the z88dk project, and HI-TECH C 7.80 is disqualified on Fasta for wrong output.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Rasm is the only other Z80 sibling, a standalone cross-assembler with an assembly-throughput claim. Pick z88dk when you need C compilers plus optimised Z80 runtime libraries, not just fast assembly of large .asm sources. The x86 siblings (Zydis, iced, Keystone, JWasm, UASM) cover other ISAs and do not compete.
verified_claims_summary: The project's wiki tables give exact Z80 cycle counts from z88dk-ticks for programs built by SDCC 4.6.0 #16608 (sdcc -mz80 --max-allocs-per-node200000) and by z88dk's zsdcc 4.6.0 #16639 and sccz80 builds, with every command line public under support/benchmarks. Against SDCC (ratios derived from page data): n-Body 1.94x with math48 and 5.07-5.40x with math32, Whetstone 2.02x and 5.13x, Fasta 1.71x and up to 3.34x, Pi 1.80x on newlib small and 3.62x on classic sccz80, Binary-Trees 1.30x (classic), Dhrystone 1.13x, Sieve 1.15x, Fannkuch 1.06x. The gains come mainly from the assembly float and 32-bit libraries.
status_note: Very active: 26,468 commits, eight commits on 2026-10-11 alone, 178 open issues and nightly builds. Usability is reference-grade because the Clarified Artistic License is not OSI-approved, but the toolchain is free to use and the benchmark sources and command lines are public, so a rebuild with symbol-based TIMER addresses for SDCC would settle the baseline windows.
